name: ANGOLA

flag.title: Flag of Angola
flag.note: Red, black & a gold machete-star emblem

lead: Angola sits on Africa's Atlantic coast and is roughly twice the size of Texas. It has one of Africa's biggest waterfalls. Its national animal is so rare that only 310 survive. Its semba dance sailed the ocean and became Brazil's samba. After 27 years of civil war, skyscrapers now rise over Luanda's bay.

facts.label: Top peak
facts.sub: In Huambo; named an Angola wonder

geo: Angola reaches from the Congo River basin to the Namib Desert. Rainforest, savanna, and dunes all fit inside. The Kwanza River flows past elephant parks to the Atlantic.
In Malanje Province, black boulders called the Pedras Negras rise 200 metres above flat savanna. Nearby, Kalandula Falls is 105 metres tall and 400 metres wide.
animals: The giant sable antelope, the palanca negra gigante, is Angola's national animal. This black bull has horns over 1.6 m long. It lives nowhere else. Civil war nearly wiped it out.
Kissama National Park shelters elephants, hippos, and crocodiles. In 2001, conservationists brought elephants in from Botswana to restock the park.
culture: Angola gave the world a dance. Semba, a close, playful partner dance, became samba in Brazil. A smoother version, kizomba, is now danced from Lisbon to Tokyo.
Meals centre on funge, a thick cassava porridge scooped up with your fingers. Moamba de galinha is chicken cooked slowly in red palm oil. Guests get food before any business talk.
history: The Kingdom of Kongo ruled northern Angola from the 1300s. Portuguese ships arrived in 1483, and the king welcomed them. His son Afonso I became one of Africa's first Christian monarchs.
Portugal ruled Angola for nearly 500 years. Independence came on 11 November 1975. Civil war began that day and lasted until 2002.
wows: Kalandula Falls is Africa's second-largest waterfall by volume.
Samba traces back to semba, carried across the Atlantic 400 years ago.
Half of Angola's people are under 16.
In 2009, a giant sable bull feared extinct was found and airlifted to safety.
Angola pumps over 1 million barrels of oil a day.
Princess Diana visited in 1997 to raise awareness of landmines.
Legend says the Pedras Negras hold warrior Queen Nzinga's footprints.

myths.myth: Only Portugal and Brazil speak Portuguese
myths.fact: More people speak Portuguese in Angola than in Portugal.

myths.myth: All diamonds come from South Africa
myths.fact: Angola, Botswana, Russia, and Canada are all big diamond miners.
